The unit text paraphrased them and listed eleven different ones. The five KICD outcomes are now restored word for word as a to e, and the designers' extra outcomes are kept but labelled as extensions (f to l) so teachers can see what is KICD and what was added. Mapping to lessons: a = L1-L2, b = L3, c = L8 (and L7 telescopes), d = L4-L6, e = L10; all five are taught and assessed (Final Explanation Parts 1-4; careers in L10 exit ticket). The teacher must confirm whether the extended outcomes should stay. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the Big Bang Theory of the origin of the universe, b) classify celestial bodies in the universe, c) outline the evolution of astrophysics and space exploration in space physics, d) explain the motion of planets around the sun, e) appreciate the careers in space exploration. Extended unit outcomes (added by the lesson designers, beyond the KICD text; the lessons teach and assess these too): f) describe the evolution of the universe, including the formation of galaxies, stars, and planetary systems, g) explain the structure and scale of the Solar System, h) apply Kepler's Laws and explain how gravitational forces govern …

phys_4_2 G1-lake-tides.issue: Lake Victoria does not have tides you can notice (only millimetres to a centimetre at most); Mombasa is now the tide example in every lesson and Lake Victoria is used as a contrast Lake Victoria does not have tides that anyone could notice or plan around. The Moon's pull is almost the same across a small body of water, so the tide-raising force (the difference in pull from one side to the other) is tiny; even the Great Lakes show lunar tides of only a few centimetres, and Lake Victoria's level is driven by rain, wind and seiches. The "fisherman in Kisumu uses the tide" story was therefore false. The lessons now use Mombasa (real, large, predictable tides, with printed tide tables) as the tide example and use Lake Victoria as an honest contrast. Every other mention (Lessons 4, 6, 7, 9, the unit storyline, the Final Explanation) was changed to match. The teacher should confirm that this change of the local example is acceptable. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL investigate how the Moon's gravitational pull produces the tides at Mombasa on the Kenyan coast, and why a lake such as Lake Victoria shows almost none.

phys_4_2 G3-storm-kenya-records.issue: The "Kenyan records" of the May 2024 storm (6-hour radio loss, Mbita reading, KMD report, Rwanda aurora) could not be verified; the lesson now uses the documented worldwide effects and asks which Kenyan services depend on the same technology (a teacher with a real Kenyan source can add it) The scenario presented invented Kenyan details as fact (a named KMD operator, Rift Valley farmers missing warnings, "unusually high tides" at Mombasa, aurora in Rwanda). It is now an openly labelled what-if. Aurora were reported in southern Africa during the May 2024 storm; the tide detail is removed because storms do not change tides. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL (This is a what-if built on the real storm; the Kenyan details are illustrative.) A radio operator at a weather station in Nairobi notices that the high-frequency radio channel used for weather and aviation messages has gone silent. Phone and ship navigation apps show positions that jump around. On social media, people in southern Africa are posting photos of coloured lights in the sky — lights normally seen only near the poles.

phys_4_2 G-incl.issue: No language or access supports existed anywhere in the unit; short supports are added in Lessons 1, 4, 6, 7 and 12 (Kiswahili key terms to be verified by a Kiswahili-speaking teacher, and more than one way to show understanding) The lesson offered only one way to show understanding (a written English paragraph). Alternatives and a few Kiswahili terms are added. The Kiswahili terms must be checked by a teacher (see the group headline). CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL as evaluative thinking requires processing time. Access options: learners may show the same understanding with a labelled diagram, an oral explanation to a partner or the teacher, or a mixed Kiswahili and English paragraph (darubini = telescope, mwanga = light, mawimbi ya redio = radio waves); read the sentence starter aloud for learners who find reading difficult.

Taifa-1 (launched April 2023) and 1KUNS-PF (2018) are real and checkable Kenyan satellites. The teacher must choose and verify the featured professionals for the folders.
